skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Control a hosted Playwright browser through inference.sh to open pages, interact with element refs, capture screenshots or video, and run JavaScript for inspection.
skill.summary: Automates browser sessions through inference.sh with element refs, screenshots, video, proxies, and JavaScript execution.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, shell templates, relative links, and /dev/null redirects. Confirmed risk remains for hosted browser capture, SOCKS proxy support, cookie extraction guidance, proxy rotation for rate-limit avoidance, and arbitrary JavaScript execution on browsed pages.

remediation.issue: Cookie extraction guidance can expose session tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the cookie extraction workflow or restrict it to owned test applications. Do not print cookies, and add explicit consent and redaction guidance.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation includes rate-limit avoidance language.
remediation.suggestion: Replace rate-limit avoidance examples with authorized geo-testing and corporate proxy examples. Add guidance to respect robots rules, terms, and request limits.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and video can capture credentials or private page data.
remediation.suggestion: Keep recording off by default, warn before use on authenticated pages, and document retention and deletion behavior for returned files.

remediation.issue: The execute function can extract sensitive DOM data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear authorized-use warning for JavaScript execution and discourage extracting secrets, cookies, tokens, or personal data.

remediation.issue: Shell templates build JSON by interpolating shell variables.
remediation.suggestion: Use a JSON builder such as jq for user-provided URLs and text values to avoid malformed requests and unintended input changes.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Sessions with Element Refs
content.value_statement: Manual browser workflows are slow to repeat and hard for agents to control. This skill routes actions through inference.sh with element refs, screenshots, video, and session state.
actual_capabilities: Open a URL in a hosted browser session and return compact element refs.
Click, fill, type, press keys, select options, scroll, drag, and upload files by ref.
Take viewport or full-page screenshots and record session video when enabled.
Run JavaScript in the current page to inspect titles, text, links, and DOM state.
Maintain browser sessions across steps and close them when work is complete.
Route browser traffic through HTTP, HTTPS, or SOCKS proxy settings.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated infsh session.
Element refs can change after navigation, form submission, or dynamic page updates.
Screenshots, video, and extracted text may contain sensitive page data.
Users are responsible for authorization, site terms, and data-handling rules.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable browser checks for login screens, forms, navigation paths, and visual states.

use_cases.title: Capture Web Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect screenshots, page text, links, and session videos for research or documentation tasks.

use_cases.title: Operate Authenticated Pages
use_cases.description: Use a persistent session to inspect dashboards and complete authorized browser actions.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target URL with agent-browser. Summarize the page title, visible interactive elements, and any elements that need a fresh snapshot.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the form URL, identify the refs for each field, fill the provided values, submit the form, and verify the result with a new snapshot.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Documentation Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Record a browser session for this workflow, use pauses between major actions, capture a full-page screenshot, and close the session to retrieve the recording.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Authorized Page Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the execute function only on the authorized page. Extract visible headings, links, and table text, then report the data sources and any sensitive fields skipped.

output_examples.input: Inspect a product settings page and identify available actions.
output_examples.output: The session opened successfully. The page contains settings tabs, save and cancel buttons, a notification toggle, and a billing link. A fresh snapshot is needed after changing tabs.

output_examples.input: Submit a contact form and capture evidence.
output_examples.output: The form was filled and submitted. The final page shows a success message, and a full-page screenshot was saved for review.

output_examples.input: Record a short workflow for documentation.
output_examples.output: The workflow was recorded from page load through the save action. The session was closed and the recording file was returned.

best_practices: Refresh the snapshot after navigation, form submission, modal changes, or dynamic content updates.
Use recording and screenshots only when the page does not show credentials or private data.
Close sessions after work completes to limit retained browser state and captured artifacts.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse old element refs after the page changes.
Do not use proxy rotation to evade rate limits or site access rules.
Do not extract cookies, tokens, passwords, or personal data from authenticated pages.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser sessions through inference.sh, including navigation, element interaction, screenshots, video, and page inspection.

faq.question: Does it require a local browser?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI and a hosted Playwright browser session.

faq.question: How are elements selected?
faq.answer: The browser snapshot returns compact refs such as @e1. Use the latest refs when clicking, filling, or selecting elements.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated sites?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are authorized. Avoid recording or extracting sensitive data from authenticated sessions.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots and video?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture screenshots and optional videos, but those artifacts may contain sensitive page content.

faq.question: Is proxy support included?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports proxy settings for authorized testing and corporate access, not for evading site controls.
